decisions.reason: As a low-risk extension of the firm’s established floor-care offer in a growing market, this product likely meets modest aspirations and can be supported by the firm’s current organisational slack.

This maintenance-oil line fits closely with the installed base of wooden floors and the firm’s system-selling logic, so absent clear underperformance management would be more likely to retain it than reallocate resources.

Although somewhat close to other care products and therefore slightly more exposed to portfolio pruning, it still reinforces the core aftercare business and is likely to be kept while results remain uncertain but not visibly poor.

A moisture-protection underlay complements the firm’s flooring systems directly, and firms with hiring, own R&D, and exposure to industry growth usually keep such adjacent products unless they clearly fall short of aspirations.
This underlay foam is a straightforward accessory tied to core floor sales, so the firm is likely to keep it as part of a complete solution offering given no evidence of disappointing performance.
As a parquet floor line very close to the firm’s established core business, it is the most strategically aligned product and therefore the least likely to be removed within the coming year.
